question: How long a break do I get if my shift is over 6 hours?
reference_answer: If daily working time is more than six hours, a worker is entitled to an uninterrupted rest break of at least 20 minutes, which they can spend away from their workstation (WTR 1998 reg. 12(1) and (3)).

question: How much time off do I need between finishing one shift and starting the next?
reference_answer: At least 11 consecutive hours' rest in each 24-hour period (12 hours for young workers) (WTR 1998 reg. 10).

question: How many days off a week am I entitled to?
reference_answer: An uninterrupted 24 hours in each 7-day period, or, if the employer chooses, two 24-hour periods or one 48-hour period in each 14 days (WTR 1998 reg. 11(1)-(2)).

question: What's the minimum wage for someone aged 19?
reference_answer: £10.85 an hour for workers aged 18 to 20 (National Minimum Wage Regulations 2015 reg. 4A(1)(b)).

question: Does my employer have to give me a payslip?
reference_answer: Yes. A worker has the right to a written itemised pay statement at or before each payment of wages, showing gross pay, deductions and their purposes, and net pay (ERA 1996 s. 8).

question: When should my employer give me my written terms and conditions?
reference_answer: The written statement of particulars must be given no later than the start of the employment (ERA 1996 s. 1(1) and (2)(b)).

question: Can my zero hours employer stop me working shifts at another restaurant?
reference_answer: No. Any term of a zero hours contract that prohibits the worker from working under another contract, or requires the employer's consent to do so, is unenforceable against the worker (ERA 1996 s. 27A).

question: Is it illegal to serve a customer a cheaper fish than the one on the menu?
reference_answer: Selling, to the purchaser's prejudice, food that is not of the nature, substance or quality demanded is an offence (Food Safety Act 1990 s. 14).

question: I live in staff accommodation at a hotel. How much of the accommodation charge can count towards my minimum wage?
reference_answer: For minimum wage purposes the accommodation offset is £11.10 for each day accommodation is provided; charges above that reduce pay when checking it meets the minimum wage (NMW Regulations 2015 regs. 14 and 16).

question: I've worked at the same pub for 3 years. How much notice does my boss have to give me?
reference_answer: At least 3 weeks: one week for each complete year of continuous employment between 2 and 12 years (ERA 1996 s. 86(1)(b)).

question: I'm 17 and do 6 hour shifts. What breaks do I get, and how long off between shifts?
reference_answer: A young worker working more than 4.5 hours is entitled to a 30-minute break (reg. 12(4)), and to 12 consecutive hours' rest in each 24-hour period (reg. 10(2)) (WTR 1998).

question: How many weeks of paid holiday does a full-time worker get in total?
reference_answer: 5.6 weeks: 4 weeks under reg. 13 plus 1.6 weeks of additional leave under reg. 13A, capped at 28 days (WTR 1998).

question: Can my employer use our tips to top our pay up to minimum wage?
reference_answer: No. Tips, gratuities and service charges paid through the employer do not count towards minimum wage pay (NMW Regulations 2015 reg. 10(m)), and qualifying tips must be allocated fairly between workers (ERA 1996 s. 27D).

question: The till was £50 short and my manager wants to take it out of my wages. Can they?
reference_answer: Only if the deduction is authorised by the contract or agreed in writing beforehand (ERA 1996 s. 13), and for workers serving the public (retail employment, s. 17) deductions for cash shortages cannot exceed one tenth of gross wages on any pay day (s. 18).

question: How much statutory sick pay will I get if I'm off ill?
reference_answer: Not answerable from the sources: statutory sick pay rates are not in the ingested legislation or guidance.

reference_answer: Not answerable from the sources: they contain current and past rates only.

question: What is the minimum wage in France?
reference_answer: Out of scope: KnowRights covers law in Great Britain only.

question: What's the best restaurant in Manchester?
reference_answer: Out of scope: KnowRights answers questions about hospitality workers' rights.

question: Breaks are only required after 8 hours, right?
reference_answer: No. The right to a rest break (at least 20 minutes) applies once daily working time is more than six hours (WTR 1998 reg. 12(1) and (3)).

question: My boss says they're allowed to keep half the tips. That's right, isn't it?
reference_answer: No. The employer must ensure the total amount of qualifying tips, gratuities and service charges is allocated fairly between workers, and amounts allocated to a worker are payable to them (ERA 1996 s. 27D(1)-(2)).

question: I'm on a zero hours contract so I don't get holiday pay, do I?
reference_answer: Wrong: zero-hours workers are entitled to statutory paid annual leave. For irregular hours workers, leave accrues at 12.07% of hours worked in each pay period (WTR 1998 reg. 15B).
